items.name: Which structured data format should I use: JSON-LD, Microdata, or RDFa?

mainEntity.name: Which structured data format should I use: JSON-LD, Microdata, or RDFa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compare JSON-LD (recommended, easiest to maintain), Microdata, and RDFa; Google accepts all three if valid, but JSON-LD is the industry standard. JSON-LD is preferred because it's embedded in <script> tags, keeps markup stable as content changes, and is easiest for developers. Key differences: JSON-LD is clean and script-based, Microdata uses HTML attributes, and RDFa is more complex. Use Google's Markup Helper or Schema.org generators for JSON-LD; plugins like Yoast support all formats. For most sites, JSON-LD is the best choice due to simplicity and tool support.

items.name: How do I get my website cited by AI search tools like Google AI Overviews?

mainEntity.name: How do I get my website cited by AI search tools like Google AI Overviews?

acceptedAnswer.text: You cannot guarantee AI tools will cite your page, but you can significantly increase the odds by structuring content with question-format headings, direct answers in the first 2–3 sentences, and structured elements like tables or lists. AI systems prefer content that is specific, credible, and easily crawlable, so include clear “what is” and “how to” headers plus FAQ schema markup. Key factors: use H2s as real questions, write answer-first paragraphs, add FAQPage/HowTo schema, and build topical clusters with internal links. Practically, draft short paragraphs with 1 supporting source per claim and verify every factual statement before publishing. While no method guarantees a citation, this approach aligns your content with how AI answer engines select and paraphrase sources.

items.name: What happens if I use AI-generated citations without checking them first?

mainEntity.name: What happens if I use AI-generated citations without checking them first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Never rely on AI-generated references without rigorous verification—spot-check 20–30% randomly and reconstruct your bibliography if you find even one fabricated source. Ask AI for verifiable sources only, require DOI/ISBN/URL, specify the citation style, and manually verify every reference before using it. Key risks: AI may invent fake authors, journals, or URLs, and hallucinate DOIs that don’t exist. Practical guidance: use tools like Citely AI to batch-check references, and only include sources you can confirm with a direct link or official identifier. Even one inaccurate citation suggests more errors exist, so treat AI citations as drafts, not final references.

items.name: How do I correctly cite AI-generated content in APA or MLA style?

mainEntity.name: How do I correctly cite AI-generated content in APA or MLA style?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cite AI as the author (omit human author), describe the prompt as the title, name the AI tool as the container, include the version, generation date, and the tool’s URL. For APA: (AI Company Name, year); for MLA: treat AI as a source with no author and use the prompt description as the title. Key factors: omit human author, use prompt as title, specify tool version, include generation date, and provide URL. Practical guidance: if you used AI for drafting or outlining, add a sentence like “This paper was produced with drafting support from Microsoft Copilot” at the start or end. Always check your instructor’s or publisher’s specific conventions before finalizing.

items.name: What’s the best prompt to ask AI for real, verifiable sources with citations?

mainEntity.name: What’s the best prompt to ask AI for real, verifiable sources with citations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use this repeatable process: define the exact claim, ask AI for real verifiable sources only, require DOI/URL/ISBN, specify citation style, verify every source manually, then use AI only to format or review. Key factors: tell AI not to guess and to state uncertainty, request both formatted citation and raw metadata, and include publisher/journal/author details. Practical guidance: prompt AI with “Find 5 credible sources… only include sources you are confident are real” and require a 1-sentence relevance summary for each. If unsure about any detail, ask AI to say so instead of hallucinating. This workflow minimizes fake citations while leveraging AI for efficiency.

items.name: When should I cite AI output versus just disclose that I used it?

mainEntity.name: When should I cite AI output versus just disclose that I used it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cite AI output when you use direct quotes, paraphrased content, images, or data from it; disclose its use as a supportive tool (e.g., for editing or outlining) with a note in the paper. Key factors: include tool name, version, generation date, URL, and describe the prompt in text or a footnote. Practical guidance: if you created a shareable chat transcript link, use that instead of the tool’s general URL. For general AI tool references, use the software template: Author (Date). Tool Name (Version) [Large language model]. URL. Disclosure is generally more suitable than citation when AI acted only as a supportive tool.
